classes.name_en: National Assembly general elections: the general seats
classes.note: Single-member territorial constituencies by plurality (Art. 51(6)(a)): 266 general seats under Art. 51(3) since 2018, 272 from 2002, 207 from 1985, 200 in 1977, and 300 in 1970. The Assembly sits five years from its first meeting unless dissolved (Art. 52); the general election falls within 60 days after the term or 90 days after a dissolution (Art. 224). Until 1997 the seats of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas were elected by their maliks; adult franchise reached them in 1997. Earlier assemblies were chosen indirectly (classes constituent_assembly and assemblies_basic_democracies).

classes.note: Under the Punjab Local Government Act 2013, union councils (a chairman and vice chairman on a joint ticket and ward councillors) and the wards of municipal committees were polled in three phases (31 October, 19 November, and 5 December 2015), and the councils then elected district chairmen and mayors. The councils were dissolved in 2019; laws of 2019, 2021, 2022, and 2025 have replaced one another without a further poll.

classes.name: سندھ بلدیاتی انتخابات
classes.name_en: Sindh local government elections (union councils and committees, town and municipal committees)
classes.note: Union councils and union committees of four wards each (Sindh LGA 2013, s. 10(4)) with a chairman and vice chairman on a joint ticket, and ward members of town and municipal committees, for four years (s. 20); mayors and chairmen are elected by the councils. Polled in three phases in 2015 and in two phases in 2022-23 (26 June 2022; 15 January 2023 for Karachi and Hyderabad divisions).

classes.note: Ward members of union councils, municipal committees, and corporations under the Balochistan Local Government Act 2010, polled on 7 December 2013 and on 29 May 2022 (Quetta and Lasbela later); district chairmen and mayors are elected by the councils.

classes.name: اسلام آباد بلدیاتی انتخابات
classes.name_en: Islamabad Capital Territory local government elections
classes.note: Union councils of the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act 2015, whose chairmen form the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad and elect its mayor; polled on 30 November 2015. Later polls were scheduled and cancelled as the number of union councils changed.

classes.name: کنٹونمنٹ بورڈز کے انتخابات
classes.name_en: Cantonment boards: elected civilian members
classes.note: Each cantonment board has members elected from its civilian wards alongside ex officio and nominated members (Cantonments Act 1924 and Cantonments Ordinance 2002); the Election Commission held the polls in 42 cantonments on 25 April 2015 and in 42 on 12 September 2021. Cantonments count among the PBS urban areas.

classes.name: مقامی حکومت آرڈیننس 2001 کے انتخابات
classes.name_en: Local governments under the Local Government Ordinances 2001: union nazims and councillors
classes.note: The devolution plan's union councils, each with a nazim and naib nazim on a joint ticket and ward councillors, elected directly on a non-party basis in five phases from 31 December 2000 to July 2001 and in two phases in August 2005; union councillors elected the district and tehsil nazims. Superseded by the provincial acts after the councils' term ended in 2009-10.

classes.name: بلدیاتی انتخابات 1979-1991
classes.name_en: Local councils under the provincial Local Government Ordinances of 1979
classes.note: Union, town, and district councils and municipal committees and corporations elected on a non-party basis in 1979, 1983, and 1987, and in some provinces 1991; dissolved in the 1990s. Held by the provincial governments, not the Election Commission.

dates.note: Elections of 1979, 1983, 1987, and 1991; not counted here.

classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of these provincial council elections was found; the provincial local government departments did not post them, and the Election Commission did not hold them.

classes.name: بنیادی جمہوریتیں
classes.name_en: Basic Democracies: union councils and their members, 1959-1969
classes.note: The Basic Democracies Order 1959 created about 80,000 directly elected members of union councils and town and union committees in East and West Pakistan (December 1959 - January 1960, and October-November 1964), who formed the electoral college for the President and the Assemblies under the 1962 Constitution; abolished with it in 1969.

dates.note: First elections, December 1959 to January 1960; not counted here.
Second elections, October and November 1964; not counted here.

classes.disposition_reason: The results were gazetted unit by unit and survive only in print; no official digital publication was found.

classes.name: قومی و صوبائی اسمبلی اور صدارتی انتخابات 1962-1965
classes.name_en: National and Provincial Assembly and presidential elections by the Basic Democrats, 1962-1965
classes.note: Under the 1962 Constitution the 80,000 Basic Democrats elected the National Assembly (April 1962 and March 1965), the Provincial Assemblies of East and West Pakistan (May 1962 and May 1965), and the President (2 January 1965, Ayub Khan against Fatima Jinnah).

dates.note: National Assembly (28 April) and Provincial Assemblies (May); not counted here.
Presidential election by the Basic Democrats.
National Assembly (March) and Provincial Assemblies (May); not counted here.

classes.name: دستور ساز اسمبلی
classes.name_en: Constituent Assemblies of 1947 and 1955, elected by the provincial assemblies
classes.note: The first Constituent Assembly was made of members elected in 1946 by the provincial legislatures of British India for the areas that became Pakistan; the second (1955) was elected by the provincial assemblies and adopted the 1956 Constitution.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the members of provincial legislatures, with no public vote; the 1946 provincial elections that seated them belong to British India's census.

classes.name: میئر، ڈسٹرکٹ چیئرمین اور ناظمین کے بالواسطہ انتخابات
classes.name_en: Mayors, district chairmen, and nazims elected by councillors
classes.note: Heads of metropolitan and municipal corporations, district councils, and (2001-2009) district and tehsil nazims are elected by the councillors (Sindh LGA 2013, s. 18 and Second Schedule; Balochistan LGA 2010; Punjab LGA 2013).
classes.disposition_reason: Votes of a few dozen councillors in each council, recorded as notifications of the returned candidate rather than as a public count.

classes.name: وزیر اعظم و وزرائے اعلیٰ کا انتخاب
classes.name_en: Prime Minister and Chief Ministers, elected by their assemblies
classes.note: The National Assembly elects the Prime Minister and each Provincial Assembly its Chief Minister by a majority of its total membership (Arts. 91(3) and 130(3)).
classes.disposition_reason: A division of the assembly's members recorded in its proceedings, not an election held by the Election Commission.

classes.name: پارٹی ٹکٹ اور انٹرا پارٹی انتخابات
classes.name_en: Party nominations and intra-party elections
classes.note: Parties issue tickets through their own boards and hold intra-party elections under their constitutions; the Commission only receives the party's certificate (Elections Act 2017, s. 208-209).
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the parties themselves; no state-run nominating contest exists.

classes.name: عدلیہ
classes.name_en: Judges
classes.note: Judges of the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and the High Courts are appointed by the President on the Judicial Commission's nomination (Arts. 175A and 175C); no judge or law-enforcement officer is elected.
classes.disposition_reason: No judicial or law-enforcement office is elected.

classes.name: بار کونسلز اور پیشہ ورانہ ادارے
classes.name_en: Bar councils, professional bodies, and student unions
classes.note: The Pakistan Bar Council and the provincial bar councils are elected by advocates, and chambers of commerce and professional councils by their members.
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of private or professional electorates run by the bodies themselves, not public elections held by the Election Commission.
